# Re-rank note 2026-11-06 (25) PROPOSAL: boundary after card 303 closed; the diagnostic-cap bug (306) goes behind the single-writer holes (298, 299) and ahead of the flaky-test bug (304); the delete-scan tooling card (305) goes last of the five, ahead of the rename

- Status: PROPOSAL, not applied. It needs an objection window (D153, D148) before the facilitator applies it.
- Why this is not a one-way door: the move is one rank edit on two unranked cards (306, 305) and one shift of 304 by one place. A later re-rank reverses it with the same placement call (rerank.py is the tool used in the dry runs). Nothing is closed, withdrawn or deleted, and both new cards are still Draft.
- Why this is not a standing-rule change: no rule, guard or head-size limit is edited. The head-size guard from re-rank 21 (at most 4 bugs above the first product card) is applied as written.
- Intent (D183): the board holds only user stories and bugs. A bug goes ahead of product work where it makes a result unsafe or dishonest. Among bugs, those that break every card's write path go first, then those that are cheap and unmasked, then those a workaround already masks. Tooling that closes a gap in a safety check goes ahead of a story only while that gap is live.
- Inputs: the card 303 retro and sign-off, the issue snapshots of 298, 299, 304, 305 and 306 (rerank-25-evidence.md), the two dry runs (rerank-25-dryruns.txt), the pre-window checklist, and the last proposal.
- Author: product manager seat, fresh Claude context (read-only reply, committed by the facilitator).

## Before (top of Ready)

298 (rank 95), 299 (96), 304 (97), 196 (98), 197 (99), 266 (100), 302 (101), 300 (102) (from the dry-run file: the proposed run shows 196 at 98 and 197 at 99 before the move). Cards 306 and 305 are unranked (rank None in the dry run).

## After (only moved and first cards)

- 95 card 298, 96 card 299 (unchanged): the vote lock and the writer lock
- 97 card 306: cap the zero-harness diagnostic like the other failure summaries
- 98 card 304: the two card-214 readiness tests pass without the thread-pool floor (one place lower)
- 99 card 305: a Codex build seat's commands go through the delete scan
- 100 card 196 and later: two places lower than the 98 it holds today, same order (dry run: 196 98 -> 100, 197 99 -> 101, 266 100 -> 102, 302 101 -> 103, 300 102 -> 104)

## Reasons, on merit

- 298 and 299 stay first. They close live holes in the single-writer rule that every card writes through, and collisions have recurred (card 299 text: index-lock, push races, a swept staged file). Nothing here outranks a live collision.
- 306 goes ahead of 304. It is unmasked: nothing hides it, and it shipped in 303's change (commit 30c9e84, per the card). Its harm is bounded, since it appears only when a run already fails, but the output is uncapped and returned on up to three attempts, and it now reaches non-endpoint tasks as well. Its three done checks are narrow and the cap is the only change, so it is cheap to take while the 303 code is fresh. A signed-off change that left a known defect should not sit behind a bug a workaround already masks.
- 306 stays behind 298 and 299 because it does no harm on a passing run and does not touch any writer.
- 304 goes after 306. The floor is kept, its recorded failure was one of two no-floor local runs (card 304 text), and CI passed both no-floor attempts. It is a real flaky-test bug (D183), but it is masked and needs a diagnosis before a fix, so it is likely a longer card. It still goes ahead of the rename, for the reason given in the last note.
- 305 goes last of the five, ahead of 196. It is tooling, not a bug, so it does not count against the guard, and it is not ahead of any bug because a hand read stands in for the scan today (the 303 sign-off re-read the 15 Codex commands by hand and found no delete). Codex quota is thin (retro: "Codex on a heavy burn"; the weekly figure is record-only), so the number of Codex build seats exposed to the gap stays small while it is open. It stays ahead of the rename because each Codex build seat widens the unscanned stretch, and the card closes a gap in a safety check, not a cosmetic one. The rename (196) is a story with no safety exposure.
- Putting 305 higher, above 306 or 304, was weighed and rejected: the hand read is a working mitigation and the quota caps use, so its urgency is lower than an unmasked defect that is already shipped.

## Head-size guard

Bugs above the first product card (196): 298, 299, 306, 304, which is 4, the guard as written (counted from the card Type fields in the evidence pack). 305 is tooling and does not count. Any further bug needs a reversal first.

## Reversals stated

- 305 moves above 306 and 304 if a Codex build seat runs a card and the hand read of its commands is skipped or cannot be done, or if a scan miss on a Codex seat is found.
- 306 moves below 304 if 304's diagnosis shows a cause that also hits the card-306 diagnostic path, or if 306 needs a second slice.
- 306 drops out of the head (to fit 3 bugs plus 305) only if another bug has to take the 4th place.

## Dry run

`rerank.py --after 299 --cards 306,304,305` (facilitator, rerank-25-dryruns.txt, no --apply) shows 306 at 97, 304 at 98, 305 at 99, and 196 at 100. The default-placement run (`rerank.py --after 298 --cards 306,305`, the same file) would put 306 at 96 and 305 at 97 ahead of 299 and 304, which this note rejects: 298 and 299 stay first.

## Not verified

- Issue states beyond the evidence-pack text; the Codex weekly limit figure (record-only, from the brief); that the delete scan stays hand-read for Codex until 305 lands (card 305 and the 303 sign-off say so, but I did not re-run it).

## Facilitator's note (not the seat's text)

The seat's dry-run line first named the comparison run `--after 303`; the facilitator's dry-run file had the same wrong label (the command that ran was `--after 298`). Both were corrected to `--after 298` before the window, and the file's output is unchanged.

### Card 298
Title: (298) A second decision run on the same checkout never votes unprotected
State: OPEN

<!-- phrase-card:298 -->

- **Status:** Draft
- **Shape:** Contract
- **Type:** bug
- **Repository:** mob-defaults (mob-crosscli: decider.py's vote lock, hold_vote_lock)
- **Source:** card 230's green 3 (bf3e4ab) named it in its own body, and the pre-ship gate (.mob/records/230/preship-gate.md, 3c) judged it a follow-up bug, not a blocker for card 230's Done check 3. decider.py creates the vote lock (mob-decider.lock in the real checkout's git dir) for one run's vote interval. A second decider run that starts while a live run holds the lock does not take it; when the first run releases the lock, the second run's vote continues with no lock, so a facilitator write during the rest of it is no longer refused and that vote can see HEAD move.
- **Depends on:** card 230 (the vote lock)
- **Actor:** decider.py's vote lock
- **Given:** two decider runs on the same checkout whose vote intervals overlap
- **Observes:** the checkout stays locked until the last overlapping vote ends (for example a holder count or one lock entry per run), and each run's record still carries equal head_start and head_end
- **Fails with:** a facilitator write refused with WriterRefused(owner="decider") at any moment while any vote on that checkout is live
- **Invariants:** card 230's tests pass; a stale lock whose process is gone is still taken over; voters stay read-only on the one checkout (working agreement: parallelism only for voting)
- **Enables:** card 216 (the default templates carry backends that work for every enabled driver)
- **One observable behaviour:** while any vote on a checkout is live, no facilitator write lands there.
- **Done checks (at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. With run A holding the lock and run B starting before A ends, a facilitator commit after A ends and before B ends is refused. ZOMBIES to be written by QA at ready.
  2. When both runs end, the lock is gone and a facilitator write succeeds. ZOMBIES to be written by QA at ready.
  3. A crashed run's lock entry is still taken over without blocking a live run's protection. ZOMBIES to be written by QA at ready.

## Context

- Filed by the facilitator on 2026-11-05 from card 230's pre-ship gate; a decision-vote safety defect, kept as a bug (D183).


### Card 299
Title: (299) A second writer on one checkout is refused across processes
State: OPEN

<!-- phrase-card:299 -->

- **Status:** Draft
- **Shape:** Contract
- **Type:** bug (flaky-is-a-bug; collisions are bugs)
- **Repository:** mob-defaults (mob-crosscli: facilitator.py Writers, the facilitator's helpers, a git hook) and avowry process tooling
- **Source:** card 230's sign-off (.mob/records/230/signoff-ctx6.md, section 2, condition 2). Card 230 shipped a single-writer lock that lives in one CardRun process's memory (facilitator.py Writers): it serialises writers inside an automated run, but a hand-run facilitator and seats writing one checkout outside a CardRun are not refused, which is the case in card 230's own source (three index-lock collisions and push races between 2026-10-30 and 2026-10-31, the swept staged file in 3c82909). It recurred twice during card 230 itself: the ready seat wrote over card 290's committed proposal in the shared avowry checkout, and at 19:46 UTC on 2026-11-04 two facilitator processes raced a push (cannot lock ref refs/heads/main). The vote lock binds only writes that go through Writers; a plain git commit during a vote is detected afterwards (exit 5), not refused.
- **Depends on:** card 230 (Writers and the vote lock)
- **Actor:** any writer to a checkout: Writers, the facilitator's helper scripts, and seats
- **Given:** a writer lock file in the checkout's git dir, taken and released like card 230's vote lock and with the same stale-lock rule
- **Observes:** a second writer, in any process, is refused with a named reason (checkout, owner, writer, operation) before it writes, and a plain `git commit` or `git push` is refused by a pre-commit and pre-push hook while another writer or a live vote holds the lock
- **Fails with:** a refusal that names the holder, instead of an index-lock collision, a ref-lock race or a swept staged file
- **Invariants:** card 230's tests pass; all writing stays serial on main in the one checkout and votes stay read-only (working agreement); a lock whose process is gone is taken over
- **Enables:** card 216 (the default templates carry the one-writer rule)
- **One observable behaviour:** two writers in two processes on one checkout never both write; the second is refused with the holder's name.
- **Done checks (at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Two processes on one checkout: the second writer's commit is refused before any git write while the first holds the lock, and succeeds after release. ZOMBIES to be written by QA at ready.
  2. A plain `git commit` and a plain `git push` are refused by the hook while a writer or a live vote holds the lock. ZOMBIES to be written by QA at ready.
  3. A stale lock (its process gone) is taken over, and a lone writer is never refused. ZOMBIES to be written by QA at ready.

## Context

- Filed by the facilitator on 2026-11-05 under card 230's sign-off condition 2; a collision defect, kept as a bug (D183). It supersedes the pre-ship gate's note that this was "a process matter for the retro".
